newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-WEAH MAY BOYCOTT FIFA AWARDS CEREMONY IN PORTUGAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WEAH MAY BOYCOTT FIFA AWARDS CEREMONY IN PORTUGAL.

text.p: AC Milan's George Weah, the 1995 FIFA world player of the year, may boycott this year's awards ceremony in Lisbon because of legal action against him by a Portuguese player he butted.
"At the moment I am not really planning to go to Lisbon on Monday," the Liberian striker said on Thursday.
"Jorge Costa has still not withdrawn his legal action and, by going to Portugal, I would face not only legal risks but also an enormous amount of local pressure."
Club sources said Weah, advised by Milan's lawyer Leandro Cantamessa, had sent a fax to FIFA general secretary Sepp Blatter requesting guarantees from Portugal.
Weah said if he had not received them by Friday morning he would not travel to Lisbon.

The fax explained that Weah, due to receive FIFA's fair play award and in the running for the 1996 player of the year award with Brazilian Ronaldo and England's Alan Shearer, did not want to create problems for the game's world governing body.
It claimed there had been suggestions from Portugal that the action be dropped in exchange for $100,000 and an official apology by the Milan striker.
"I have apologised to Costa informally and been suspended for six matches. What more do they want?" said Weah.
He promised on Friday he would publish the fax sent to Blatter as well as one received from Costa's lawyers on Wednesday and alleged to contain compensation proposals.
Last month Weah apologised to FIFA for the "moment of craziness" which led to his six-match ban for butting Costa in a European Champions' League match in Portugal.
Weah said then in a letter to Blatter he wanted to "extend his deepest regrets" over the incident.
FIFA chairman Joao Havelange said he wanted to present Weah with the fair play award personally.
"FIFA has named the Liberian for its 1996 Fair Play award and it is not going to change its decision," Havelange said in a newspaper interview last month.
"A reaction, provoked, cannot erase 10 years of loyalty everywhere and in every competition.
"I will be happy to give him the award personally on January 20 in Lisbon and I'm confident that Costa himself will be there beside me on that day to shake his hand."
Porto's captain suffered a broken nose when he tangled with Weah in the players' tunnel after the match on November 20. Weah alleged Costa had provoked him with racist gestures.
If Weah does decide to skip the FIFA awards ceremony, held in Milan last year, he may also be forced by the same reasons to miss an all-star match between Africa and Europe.
That match, the first between representative teams from the two continents and widely seen as a reply to racism, is scheduled to be held in Lisbon on January 29.
